title: How people are paid
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:40Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point covers types of work (full-time, part-time, casual, unpaid) rather than the methods of payment (hourly wages, salary, commission, piece rates), so it teaches a different idea.

draft.title: How people are paid
card: a set rate for each hour worked. Pay rises or falls with the hours, so a worker who does more hours earns more.
a set amount for the year, usually paid in equal parts such as fortnightly. The pay stays the same even if the hours change a little.
a payment based on the value of what a worker sells, often a percentage of sales. More sales mean more pay.
a set payment for each item a worker makes. More items made mean more pay.
draft.remember: Wages pay for hours, salary pays for the year, commission pays for sales and piece rates pay for items made.

a.q: Jai is paid $4 for every cap he sews at a factory. Which way is he paid?
a.why: Jai is paid for each item he makes, which is a piece rate. Commission is tempting because pay depends on output, but commission is based on the value of sales, not items made.
a.clue: What is Jai paid for: hours, sales or items made?

b.q: Priya sells cars in Newcastle and earns 3% of the value of every car she sells. In a quiet month she sells no cars. What is true of her pay?
opts: It is commission, so it falls when sales fall
It is a salary, so it stays the same each month
It is a piece rate, so it depends on items made
It is wages, so it depends on the hours she works
b.why: Priya is paid a percentage of the value of her sales, which is commission, so her pay falls when she sells less. A piece rate is tempting because she sells items, but a piece rate is paid for items made, not a share of sales value.
b.clue: Look at what her 3% is taken from.

b.best: It is commission, so it falls when sales fall
